Longsword is the modern name for the large late-medieval European sword with a grip long enough for two hands. Its straight double-edged blade could cut and thrust.

Fencing manuals from the 1300s and 1400s, including those of Fiore dei Liberi, record how it was used: cuts, thrusts, grappling at close range, and gripping the blade partway along to stab through gaps in armour.
